issues.description: Field 'numberOfTutors': the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares numberOfTutors as int, but the solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the field as short and uses short for the constructor parameter and the setter parameter while the getter method signature returns int. This mismatch between the UML and the solution (and the mixed use of short vs int inside the solution) is confusing for students: they cannot tell which primitive type is expected (int per UML or short per implementation), and tests or instructor expectations based on the UML may disagree with the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the UML: change the field type in the solution to int and use int consistently for the constructor parameter and the setter parameter (i.e., declare 'private int numberOfTutors;', constructor parameter 'int numberOfTutors', and setter parameter 'int numberOfTutors'). Keep the getter returning int. Alternatively, if short was intended, update the problem statement UML to show 'short' for numberOfTutors — but prefer aligning the solution to the UML (int) to avoid student confusion.
